mainTopic: Wicked kings and commoners of Tanach: their sins, who loses עולם הבא, and the great power of feeding guests
overview: This amud opens by finishing a quote from תהלים about ה׳'s rewards for one who loves Him. Then ריש לקיש explains why the ע in רְשָׁעִים hangs above the line: one who is poor below is poor above. The ע is still written to protect the honor of דוד or נחמיה. Next the גמרא discusses the wicked kings, who were great Torah scholars, and lists those with no share in עולם הבא, including אבשלום. It then describes how אחז, מנשה and אמון each went further than the king before him in idol worship, in attacks on the Temple and the תורה, and in עריות. יהויקים went further still, claiming people do not need God at all. רבא asks why יהויקים is not on the list of those who lose עולם הבא, and the answer given is about מיכה instead: he made an idol, but he was protected because he fed travelers. This leads to רבי יוחנן's teachings on the great power of giving food, and the explanation of his list begins at the end of the amud.

steps.title: Finishing the quote from תהלים: the rewards of trusting ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes a quotation from תהלים צ״א that began earlier on the daf, describing ה׳'s promises to one who loves Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Because he desired Me, I will save him. I will raise him up because he knows My name. He will call Me and I will answer him. I am with him in trouble; I will rescue him and honor him. I will satisfy him with long life and show him My salvation."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a long quote from תהלים that started before this section. These verses close out the earlier discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued here. The verses list ה׳'s rewards for someone who attaches himself to Him: rescue, honor, long life and salvation. It is the closing line of the earlier topic, not the start of a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: desired, longed for (here: longed for ה׳)
I will raise him up / protect him on high

phrases.english: "Because he has desired Me, I will deliver him;
I will set him on high, because he has known My name.
He shall call upon Me, and I will answer him;
I am with him in trouble;
I will rescue him and honor him.
With long life I will satisfy him,
and show him My salvation."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes a quotation from תהלים that began earlier on the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ה׳ promises rescue, honor, long life and salvation to one who loves Him and knows His name.

steps.title: Why the ע in רְשָׁעִים hangs above the line
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש explains that the raised ע in a verse in איוב hints that the word can be read רָשִׁים, 'poor ones,' teaching that one who is poor below is poor above.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: What does the verse mean, "Their light will be withheld from the wicked, and the high arm will be broken"? Why is the ע of רְשָׁעִים hanging? Because once a person becomes poor down here, he becomes poor up in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי שמעון בן לקיש points out an unusual letter in a verse in איוב and explains what it teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the written text of איוב, the ע of רְשָׁעִים is written raised above the other letters. If you set it aside, the word reads רָשִׁים, 'poor people.' רבי שמעון בן לקיש reads this as a hint: a person who is 'poor' and lowly in this world is also considered lowly in Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the meaning of what is written
hanging, written raised above the line

steps.confusionAlert: The verse is not changing its plain meaning about the wicked. The raised letter adds an extra hint on top of the simple reading.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"And their light will be withheld from the wicked,
phrases.notes: איוב 38:15

phrases.english: and the high arm shall be broken"?

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה עַיִן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים תְּלוּיָה?
phrases.english: For what reason is the ayin of "resha'im" suspended?
phrases.notes: The ע is written raised above the line. Set it aside and the word reads רָשִׁים, which means 'poor people.'

phrases.english: Once a person becomes poor below,
he becomes poor above.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about a verse in איוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The raised ע in רְשָׁעִים hints at רָשִׁים: one who becomes poor below becomes poor above.

steps.title: Then why write the ע at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the verse wants to say רָשִׁים, it should leave out the ע completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the ע not be written at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי שמעון בן לקיש's reading. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the message is 'poor people,' the simplest way would be to write רָשִׁים with no ע. Writing the ע, even raised, keeps the plain meaning 'wicked.' So why did the verse keep it?

keyTerms.meaning: then let it not be written at all

phrases.english: Then let it not be written at all!
phrases.notes: Meaning: if the point is 'poor people,' just write רָשִׁים and drop the ע completely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן לקיש's reading of the raised ע as hinting רָשִׁים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the intended word is רָשִׁים, the ע should have been left out entirely rather than written raised.

steps.title: The ע stays to protect the honor of דוד or נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר answer that the ע is kept to protect the honor of a great צדיק: one says דוד, the other says נחמיה בן חכליה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree. One says: it is kept because of the honor of דוד. The other says: because of the honor of נחמיה בן חכליה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question from the last step. Each names a different righteous person whose honor the ע protects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse said only רָשִׁים, it would sound as if every lowly or troubled person is lowly in Heaven too. Keeping the ע softens this, so the hint does not reflect badly on great people like דוד or נחמיה who also went through hard times. We are not told which אמורא held which opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: one said... and one said (two opinions, not saying who held which)
נחמיה, leader of the return to ירושלים

steps.whatToRemember: The raised ע in רְשָׁעִים hints at 'poor ones,' but the ע is still written so as not to shame righteous people like דוד or נחמיה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר, מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל דָּוִד;
phrases.english: One said: because of the honor of David;
phrases.notes: Without the ע, the verse could sound like it puts down a righteous person who had hard times, like דוד.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר, מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל נְחֶמְיָה בֶּן חֲכַלְיָה.
phrases.english: and one said: because of the honor of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the text is written the way it is: the ע is kept for the sake of a righteous person's honor
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ע should be left out completely if the hint is רָשִׁים
steps.terutzMaskana: The ע is written, but raised, to protect the honor of דוד (one view) or נחמיה (other view)

steps.title: The wicked kings were great Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that מנשה knew 55 ways of explaining תורת כהנים, אחאב knew 85, and ירבעם knew 103.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: מנשה used to study 55 ways of explaining תורת כהנים, matching the years he was king. אחאב knew 85, and ירבעם knew 103.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins with a ברייתא about the Torah knowledge of the wicked kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These kings are known as great sinners, yet the ברייתא shows they were very learned. מנשה's 55 ways match his 55 years as king. אחאב knew more, and ירבעם knew the most.

keyTerms.meaning: ספר ויקרא and its halachic midrash

steps.confusionAlert: Being wicked did not mean these kings were ignorant. The ברייתא stresses that they were great scholars.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Manasseh would study
fifty-five ways of explaining Torat Kohanim,
phrases.notes: תורת כהנים is ספר ויקרא, together with its midrash on the halachos.

phrases.english: corresponding to the years of his reign.
Ahab: eighty-five;
Jeroboam: one hundred and three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the wicked kings' Torah learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנשה knew 55 ways of explaining תורת כהנים (matching his years as king), אחאב 85, and ירבעם 103.

steps.title: אבשלום has no share in the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי מאיר learns from a double wording in a פסוק that אבשלום was killed in this world and also lost עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר used to say, אבשלום has no share in the World to Come, because it says 'they struck אבשלום and killed him.' 'They struck him' means in this world, and 'killed him' means in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר adds אבשלום to the list of people who lose עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two verbs, 'struck' and 'killed.' רבי מאיר reads them as two different deaths. One is the death of the body in this world, and the other is losing the next world.

keyTerms.meaning: A share in the World to Come

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir used to say,

phrases.aramaic: אַבְשָׁלוֹם אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: Absalom has no share in the World to Come,
as it says: 'And they struck Absalom and killed him.'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב׳ 18:15.

phrases.english: 'And they struck him': in this world,
'and they killed him': for the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another person to the list of those who lose עולם הבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבשלום has no share in עולם הבא, learned from the double wording 'struck' and 'killed.'

steps.title: The wicked kings neither live nor are judged
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, quoting רבי מאיר, says אחז, אחזיה and the kings of ישראל described as doing evil are neither brought to life in עולם הבא nor judged in גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי מאיר: אחז, אחזיה, and all the kings of ישראל about whom it is written 'he did evil in the eyes of ה׳' do not live in the World to Come, and they are not judged in גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא gives a group of wicked kings a special in-between outcome: no עולם הבא, but also no punishment in גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not the same as the earlier list of people who simply 'have no share.' These kings are not rewarded with life, but they are also not sentenced. The phrase 'he did evil in the eyes of ה׳' is the sign that tells us which kings are included.

keyTerms.meaning: He did evil in the eyes of ה׳, a phrase used about many kings
They neither live (in עולם הבא) nor are judged (in גיהנם)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not judged' does not mean they are fine. It means they get neither reward nor punishment in the next world.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Meir,
Ahaz and Ahaziah and all the kings of Israel
about whom it is written 'and he did evil in the eyes of the Lord':
they neither live nor are judged.
phrases.notes: He means they don't come to life in עולם הבא, and they aren't sentenced to גיהנם either.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא from רבי מאיר's school, about a different group with a different outcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kings described as 'doing evil in the eyes of ה׳' neither live in עולם הבא nor are judged in גיהנם.

steps.title: מנשה's innocent blood: the view in בבל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that מנשה filled ירושלים with innocent blood. In בבל they explain this as his killing of ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'מנשה also spilled a great deal of innocent blood, until he filled ירושלים from end to end, besides his sin of making יהודה sin by doing evil in the eyes of ה׳.' Here in בבל they explain this to mean that he killed ישעיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to מנשה and asks what 'filled ירושלים with innocent blood' means. The scholars of בבל answer: he killed the נביא ישעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Killing one person does not literally fill a city with blood. The view in בבל holds that killing a great צדיק like ישעיה counts as that much bloodshed. The next step gives a second view.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'mouth to mouth', meaning from end to end

phrases.aramaic: ״וְגַם דָּם נָקִי שָׁפַךְ מְנַשֶּׁה הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד
phrases.english: 'And also Manasseh shed a very great amount of innocent blood
phrases.notes: מלכים ב׳ 21:16.

phrases.aramaic: עַד אֲשֶׁר מִלֵּא אֶת יְרוּשָׁלִַים פֶּה לָפֶה
phrases.english: until he filled Jerusalem from end to end,

phrases.aramaic: לְבַד מֵחַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר הֶחֱטִיא אֶת יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: besides his sin in which he made Judah sin,
to do evil in the eyes of the Lord.'
Here they explain it: that he killed Isaiah.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means בבל, where this גמרא was learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to מנשה, who was mentioned in step 5, and explains a פסוק about his crimes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In בבל, 'innocent blood' is explained as מנשה's killing of ישעיה.

steps.title: מנשה's innocent blood: the view in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they explain that מנשה made an idol so heavy that a thousand people carried it, and every day it killed all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: In ארץ ישראל they say: he made an idol that took a thousand people to carry, and every single day he killed all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of the same פסוק, from the scholars of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'innocent blood' is read more literally, as huge numbers of people dying. Each day a new thousand people died carrying the heavy idol, so the blood truly filled ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
A load or burden to carry

phrases.english: In the West they say:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעָשָׂה צֶלֶם מַשּׂאוֹי אֶלֶף בְּנֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: that he made an idol that was a load for a thousand people,
and each and every day he would kill all of them.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't; the meaning is the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second explanation of the same פסוק, different from the one in בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל, 'innocent blood' means the thousands who died daily carrying מנשה's idol.

steps.title: Whose view matches רבה בר בר חנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the two views fits רבה בר בר חנה's teaching that one צדיק's soul equals the whole world.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this teaching of רבה בר בר חנה follow: 'The soul of one צדיק is equal to the entire world'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a well-known teaching and asks which of the two explanations it fits with. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two views argue about what 'filled ירושלים' means: one person, or thousands of people. רבה בר בר חנה's idea about the huge worth of a צדיק could support one of them.

phrases.english: Whose view does this follow,
that Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
The soul of one righteous person is equal
to the entire world?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects an outside teaching to the argument between בבל and ארץ ישראל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which explanation of מנשה's 'innocent blood' fits רבה בר בר חנה's teaching.

steps.title: It matches the view that he killed ישעיה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה's teaching fits the view that מנשה killed ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows the one who says that he killed ישעיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the teaching fits the view from בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one צדיק is worth the whole world, then killing ישעיה alone can be described as filling ירושלים with blood. That explains how one killing could be called so much bloodshed.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: Two views on מנשה's 'innocent blood': בבל says he killed ישעיה, and ארץ ישראל says his idol killed a thousand people a day. רבה בר בר חנה's teaching that one צדיק equals the world fits the view about ישעיה.

phrases.english: According to the one who says he killed Isaiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The teaching fits the view that מנשה killed ישעיה, since one צדיק equals the whole world.

steps.title: One idol or many idols?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that one פסוק says מנשה made a פסל (one idol) and another says פסילים (idols).
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'an idol,' and it is also written 'idols.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that two פסוקים about מנשה seem to disagree on whether he made one idol or many. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is a contradiction between two פסוקים. If there was only one idol, why does the other פסוק use the plural?

keyTerms.meaning: It is written... and it is also written (pointing out two פסוקים that seem to clash)

phrases.english: It is written 'an idol,'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב׳ 33:7.

phrases.english: and it is written 'idols.'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב׳ 33:19.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from מנשה's idol to a contradiction in how the פסוקים describe it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two descriptions of מנשה's idol
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק uses the singular and another uses the plural, so they seem to clash.

steps.title: One idol with four faces
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן: at first the idol had one face, and later מנשה gave it four faces so the שכינה would see it from every side and be angered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: At first he made it with one face, and in the end he made it with four faces, so that the שכינה would see it and become angry.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן settles the contradiction. It was one idol, but it changed from one face to four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'פסל' describes the one idol as it was at first. 'פסילים' describes it after it had four faces, which made it look like many idols. The four faces were meant to anger the שכינה from every direction.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
At first he made it one face,
and in the end he made it four faces,
so that the Divine Presence would see and become angry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּתְּחִלָּה עָשָׂה לוֹ פַּרְצוּף אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two stages of time: each פסוק describes the idol at a different stage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים seem to disagree about whether there was one idol or many.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was one idol that later had four faces, so both the singular and the plural are correct.

steps.title: The idol moves deeper into the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: אחז placed the idol in the upper chamber, מנשה placed it in the היכל, and אמון brought it into the קדש הקדשים. Each step is backed by a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחז set it up in the upper chamber, as it says: 'the altars on the roof of אחז's upper chamber.' מנשה set it up in the היכל, as it says: 'he placed the carved אשרה in the House about which ה׳ told דוד and שלמה his son: in this House and in ירושלים, which I chose from all the tribes of ישראל, I will place My Name forever.' אמון brought it into the קדש הקדשים, as it says: 'For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the cover too narrow to wrap oneself in.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the idol worship got worse with each king. Each one placed the idol in a holier part of the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three stages: the upper chamber (אחז), the היכל itself (מנשה), and finally the קדש הקדשים (אמון). Each stage is proven from a פסוק. The פסוק in ישעיהו about a crowded bed is read as hinting at the idol in the holiest room.

keyTerms.meaning: The main hall of the בית המקדש
The Holy of Holies, the holiest room
A tree or pole used for idol worship

steps.whatToRemember: The idol went step by step deeper into the בית המקדש: אחז put it in the upper chamber, מנשה in the היכל, and אמון in the קדש הקדשים.

phrases.english: Ahaz set it up in the upper chamber,
as it says: 'And the altars that were on the roof
of the upper chamber of Ahaz, etc.'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב׳ 23:12.

phrases.english: Manasseh set it up in the Sanctuary,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיָּשֶׂם אֶת פֶּסֶל הָאֲשֵׁרָה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה בַּבַּיִת
phrases.english: as it says: 'And he placed the carved image of the asherah that he made in the House
phrases.notes: מלכים ב׳ 21:7.

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר אָמַר ה׳ אֶל דָּוִד וְאֶל שְׁלֹמֹה [בְנוֹ]
phrases.english: about which the Lord said to David and to Solomon his son:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording, matching the פסוק.

phrases.english: In this House and in Jerusalem,
which I chose from all the tribes of Israel,
I will place My Name forever.'
Amon brought it into the Holy of Holies,
as it says: 'For the bed is too short to stretch out on,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 28:20. The גמרא reads this פסוק as a hint to the idol being in the holiest room.

phrases.english: 'and the cover is too narrow to wrap oneself in.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues talking about the idol, now describing where each king placed it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The idol was moved step by step into holier places: the upper chamber (אחז), the היכל (מנשה), and the קדש הקדשים (אמון).

steps.title: What does 'the bed is too short for spreading' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'כי קצר המצע מהשתרע' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'For the bed is too short for spreading'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of a phrase from a פסוק in ישעיה. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 quoted this פסוק as the proof that אמון brought the idol into the קדש הקדשים. Now the גמרא asks what the words of that פסוק actually mean.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "For the bed is too short for spreading"?
phrases.notes: ישעיה 28:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After describing the idol placed in the Temple, the גמרא turns to a פסוק it reads as describing that idol.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'כי קצר המצע מהשתרע'.

steps.title: The bed cannot hold two companions
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains that the 'bed' (the Temple) is too narrow for two companions, God and the idol, to rule over it together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: This bed is too short for two companions to rule over it together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן answers the question. The 'bed' is the בית המקדש, and it cannot hold both God and an idol at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the word מהשתרע as two words joined together: 'to rule' (להשתרר) and 'companions' (רעים). So the פסוק is saying the Temple has no room for two to rule there, and once the idol is brought in, the שכינה cannot stay.

keyTerms.meaning: To rule over, to take control

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
[For] this bed is too short
to have rule over it
two companions together.
phrases.notes: He hears the word מהשתרע as 'rule' plus 'רעים', companions: God and the idol can't share one place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Temple cannot have two 'companions', God and an idol, ruling in it together.

steps.title: What does 'the covering is too narrow' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the second half of the פסוק, 'והמסכה צרה', means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'And the covering is too narrow, etc.'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of the same פסוק and asks what it means. This sets up רבי יונתן's emotional explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning is a blanket too narrow to wrap up in. The words מסכה and צרה can also mean 'molten idol' and 'rival wife', and the answer will use those meanings.

keyTerms.meaning: A covering, and also a molten idol
Narrow, and also a rival (a co-wife)

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "And the covering is too narrow, etc."?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק, now its second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'והמסכה צרה' in the פסוק.

steps.title: רבי יונתן cried over this פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן would cry at this פסוק: how could an idol be made a 'rival' to the One who gathers the waters of the sea?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: When רבי יונתן reached this פסוק he would cry. About the One of whom it is written 'He gathers the waters of the sea like a heap,' should an idol be made into His rival?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by telling that רבי יונתן would cry at this פסוק. He read it as saying that an idol was set up as a 'rival' to God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads מסכה as 'idol' and צרה as 'rival wife'. The word כהתכנס at the end of the פסוק points to the פסוק 'כונס כנד מי הים', which describes God's great power. The pain is that people made a lowly idol into God's competitor in His own house.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן כִּי הֲוָה מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא
phrases.english: When Rabbi Yonatan would reach this verse
he would cry:
The One about whom it is written
"He gathers the waters of the sea like a heap"
phrases.notes: תהלים 33:7. The word כונס matches כהתכנס at the end of the פסוק in ישעיה.

phrases.english: should an idol be made into a rival to Him?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן כִּי הֲוָה מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא הֲוָה קָא בָכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The idol (מסכה) was made a rival (צרה) to the all-powerful God, which made רבי יונתן cry.

steps.title: How each king attacked the Temple service and the תורה
steps.stepSummary: אחז stopped the Temple service and sealed the תורה; מנשה cut out God's Names and destroyed the מזבח; אמון burned the תורה and offered a lizard on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחז stopped the Temple service and sealed up the תורה, as it says: 'Bind up the testimony, seal the תורה among My students.' מנשה cut out the written Names of God and tore down the מזבח. אמון burned the תורה and brought a lizard up onto the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new list showing how each of the three kings went one step further than the king before him in sinning against the Temple and the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as step 14, where each king brought the idol deeper into the Temple. Here אחז stops the service, מנשה destroys the מזבח itself, and אמון makes it impure with an impure creature, while the attack on the תורה grows from sealing it to cutting it to burning it.

keyTerms.meaning: A lizard, an impure creeping animal

phrases.english: [Achaz stopped the Temple service],
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

phrases.english: and sealed up the Torah,
as it is said: "Bind up the testimony,
seal the Torah among My students."
phrases.notes: ישעיה 8:16

phrases.english: Menashe cut out the written Names of God,
and tore down the altar.
Amon burned the Torah,
and brought a lizard up onto the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the pattern of step 14, where each king went further than the one before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each king's sin against the Temple and the תורה was worse than the one before: sealing, then cutting, then burning.

steps.title: How each king went further in עריות
steps.stepSummary: אחז permitted forbidden relations, מנשה lived with his sister, and אמון lived with his mother, as hinted by 'אמון increased guilt.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אחז permitted forbidden relations. מנשה lived with his sister. אמון lived with his mother, as it says: 'For he, אמון, increased guilt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same three kings are listed again, this time for sins of עריות, and once again each one goes further than the one before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחז only declared these relations permitted, מנשה acted on it with his sister, and אמון did the worst thing, with his own mother. The פסוק saying אמון 'increased guilt' is brought as the source that his sin was greater than all the others.

phrases.english: Achaz permitted forbidden relations.
Menashe had relations with his sister.
Amon had relations with his mother,
as it is said: "For he, Amon, increased guilt."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 33:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second list in the same style, now about עריות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In עריות too, each king went further: אחז permitted it, מנשה did it with his sister, and אמון did it with his mother.

steps.title: What was אמון's 'increased guilt'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue: one says אמון's great guilt was burning the תורה, the other says it was living with his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree. One says it means he burned the תורה, and one says it means he lived with his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת about what the פסוק 'הרבה אשמה' refers to. Both sins were mentioned in the lists above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that אמון was the worst, but they argue which of his sins the פסוק is pointing to. The step does not say which רב holds which view.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not tell us which view belongs to רבי יוחנן and which to רבי אלעזר; it only says 'one said... and one said...'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar disagree:
One said: It means that he burned the Torah,
and one said: It means that he had relations with his mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a disagreement about how to read the פסוק quoted in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'הרבה אשמה' refers either to burning the תורה or to living with his mother.

steps.title: אמון's answer to his mother
steps.stepSummary: אמון's mother asked what pleasure he could get from her, and he answered that he did it only to anger his Creator.
steps.simpleTranslation: His mother said to him: Do you get any pleasure from the place you came out of? He said to her: I am only doing this to anger my Creator.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing how wicked אמון was. He did not even sin for pleasure, only to anger God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why his guilt was 'increased': the sin was done purely as rebellion against God. It continues the theme from step 13, where מנשה made the idol four-faced so the שכינה would see it and be angered.

phrases.english: His mother said to him:
Do you get any pleasure
from the place you came out of?
He said to her: I am not doing this
except to anger my Creator.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story that shows the depth of אמון's sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אמון sinned only to anger God, not for pleasure.

steps.title: יהויקים: we don't even need God's light
steps.stepSummary: יהויקים claimed the kings before him did not know how to anger God; since they had shining gold, God could take back His light.
steps.simpleTranslation: When יהויקים came, he said: The kings before me did not know how to anger God. What do we need Him for except His light? We have shining פרוים gold that we use; let Him take back His light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a later king, יהויקים, who boasted that he would anger God even more than the kings before him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kings before him rebelled through idols and sins, but יהויקים claims to reject God completely. He says the only thing they need from God is light, and their special shining gold can replace even that.

keyTerms.meaning: The earlier ones, those before me
פרוים gold, a special shining gold

phrases.english: When Yehoyakim came, he said:
The earlier kings did not know how to anger God.
Do we need Him for anything except His light?
We have parvayim gold
that we use for light;
let Him take away His light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from אמון to a later king who claims to be even more defiant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהויקים claimed his shining gold made God's light unnecessary.

steps.title: But the gold belongs to God
steps.stepSummary: The people challenged יהויקים: silver and gold belong to God, as חגי says.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But silver and gold are His, as it says: 'Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold, says ה׳ צבאות'!
steps.whatsHappening: The people push back against יהויקים. His gold is no replacement for God, because the gold itself belongs to God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This attacks the base of his claim. If the gold is God's, then using it to replace God's light still depends on God.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא,
phrases.english: They said to him: But silver and gold are His,
as it is said: "Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold,
says the Lord of hosts"?
phrases.notes: חגי 2:8

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges יהויקים's claim from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: יהויקים's claim that his gold makes God unnecessary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The gold itself belongs to God, as the פסוק in חגי says.

steps.title: יהויקים: God already gave the earth to us
steps.stepSummary: יהויקים answered that God already gave the earth and its gold to people, as תהלים says.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: He already gave it to us, as it says: 'The heavens are the heavens of ה׳, but the earth He gave to people.'
steps.whatsHappening: יהויקים twists a פסוק to answer them. He claims God gave the earth away, so the gold now belongs to people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees the gold was once God's but says it was handed over, so they no longer depend on God. The גמרא presents this as the height of his defiance: he uses the תורה's own words to push God away.

keyTerms.meaning: He already gave it to us

steps.whatToRemember: The kings got worse and worse: אחז, מנשה and אמון each went further in idolatry, in sins against the תורה and Temple, and in עריות, and אמון sinned only to anger God. יהויקים went further still, claiming people don't need God at all.

phrases.english: He said to them: He already gave it to us,
as it is said: "The heavens are the heavens of the Lord,
but the earth He gave to people."
phrases.notes: תהלים 115:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: יהויקים answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the gold was God's but was given over to people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the gold belongs to God, people still depend on Him.
steps.terutzMaskana: יהויקים claims the earth and its gold were handed to people, so they can do without God.

steps.title: Why is יהויקים not on the list?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רבה בר מרי why the תנאים did not count יהויקים among the kings who have no share in עולם הבא, since a verse describes his disgusting acts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רבה בר מרי: Why didn't they list יהויקים? After all, the verse speaks of his abominations and 'what was found on him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question: יהויקים seems as wicked as the kings on the list, so why is he missing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists only certain kings as losing עולם הבא. רבא brings a verse showing that יהויקים did abominable things. That makes his absence from the list puzzling.

keyTerms.meaning: and what was found on him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי:
phrases.english: Rava said to Rabba bar Mari:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא מָנוּ אֶת יְהוֹיָקִים?
phrases.english: For what reason did they not list Yehoyakim?
phrases.notes: He means: why isn't he on the משנה's list of kings with no share in עולם הבא?

phrases.english: Since it is written about him:
"And the rest of the acts of Yehoyakim
and his abominations that he did
and that which was found on him."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 36:8

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא מָנוּ אֶת יְהוֹיָקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After describing יהויקים's defiant words, רבא asks why he is not on the list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason יהויקים is left off the list of kings with no share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: What does 'found on him' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops to ask what the unclear phrase 'that which was found on him' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'that which was found on him' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: Before going on, the גמרא asks for the meaning of the strange phrase in the verse. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse hints at something shameful 'found on' יהויקים but does not say what it was. The גמרא wants it spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: what is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is "and that which was found on him"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the meaning of the verse quoted in the previous step.

steps.title: What was etched on יהויקים's body
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue: one says he engraved the name of an idol on his private organ, the other says he engraved the name of God there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר: one said he carved the name of an idol on his private organ, and one said he carved the name of Heaven on his private organ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר about what was found on his body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view: it showed his devotion to עבודה זרה. The other view: carving God's name there was an act of terrible contempt. Either way, it shows how wicked he was, which makes רבא's question even stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of Heaven, God's name

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: שֶׁחָקַק שֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה עַל אַמָּתוֹ,
phrases.english: One says: that he carved the name of an idol on his private organ,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: שֶׁחָקַק שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל אַמָּתוֹ.
phrases.english: and one says: that he carved the name of Heaven on his private organ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the verse's wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the name of an idol or the name of God was carved on his body.

steps.title: No answer for kings, but an answer for מיכה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי says he never heard a reason about the kings, but he did hear why מיכה is not listed among regular people: he fed travelers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About kings I didn't hear, but about regular people I heard. Why didn't they list מיכה? Because his bread was available to travelers, as it says: 'everyone who passes by and returns to the Levites.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר מרי admits he has no tradition about יהויקים. Instead, he shares a similar answer about מיכה, a regular person who made an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question about יהויקים stays unanswered. But we learn a parallel idea: מיכה, who made an idol, was not listed because he was generous to guests. Kindness to travelers was a strong enough merit to keep him off the list.
steps.whatToRemember: מיכה made an idol, yet his generous hospitality kept him off the list of those who lose עולם הבא.

phrases.english: He said to him: Concerning kings, I did not hear,
concerning regular people, I heard.
phrases.notes: The משנה also lists regular people, not just kings, who lose עולם הבא.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא מָנוּ אֶת מִיכָה?
phrases.english: For what reason did they not list Michah?
Because his bread was available to travelers,
as it says: "Everyone who passes by and returns to the Levites."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבא's question by saying he has no answer about kings and offering a parallel case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer about יהויקים; מיכה was left off because of his hospitality.

steps.title: מיכה's idol crossed the sea
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the 'trouble' passing through the sea in a verse from זכריה refers to מיכה's idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And trouble will pass through the sea, and He will strike the waves in the sea.' רבי יוחנן said: This is the idol of מיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues talking about מיכה and brings רבי יוחנן's reading of a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'trouble' that went through the sea is understood as מיכה's idol. It came along with the Jewish people when they crossed the sea, showing how early this idol began.

phrases.english: "And trouble shall pass through the sea
and He shall strike the waves in the sea."
phrases.notes: זכריה 10:11

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זֶה פִּסְלוֹ שֶׁל מִיכָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: This is the idol of Michah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זֶה פִּסְלוֹ שֶׁל מִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more about מיכה, the person just mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'trouble' crossing the sea in זכריה is מיכה's idol.

steps.title: The smoke of the altar and the idol mixed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי נתן says מיכה's town גרב was only three מיל from שילה, so the smoke of the altar and of the idol mixed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי נתן says: From גרב to שילה was three מיל, and the smoke of the altar fire and the smoke of מיכה's idol would mix with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא showing how close מיכה's idol worship was to the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is how shocking the situation was: idol worship went on right next to the place of God's service. This sets up the next steps about why מיכה was not destroyed and why the people were punished.

keyTerms.meaning: the arranged wood fire on the altar

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
From Garev to Shiloh was three mil,
phrases.notes: גרב was where מיכה lived; שילה was where the משכן stood then.

phrases.english: and the smoke of the altar fire
and the smoke of Michah's idol
would mix with each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues describing מיכה's idol and how close it was to the משכן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מיכה's idol was so close to שילה that their smoke mixed.

steps.title: God protects מיכה for his hospitality
steps.stepSummary: The angels wanted to push מיכה out of the world, but God told them to leave him because he fed travelers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ministering angels wanted to push him away. God said to them: Leave him alone, because his bread is available to travelers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how the angels wanted to destroy מיכה, and God stopped them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with idol smoke mixing with the altar's smoke, מיכה's kindness to travelers protected him. This matches the reason given earlier for leaving him off the list.

keyTerms.meaning: to push him away (remove him from the world)

phrases.english: The ministering angels wanted to push him away.
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them:

phrases.aramaic: הַנִּיחוּ לוֹ, שֶׁפִּתּוֹ מְצוּיָה לְעוֹבְרֵי דְּרָכִים.
phrases.english: Leave him, because his bread is available to travelers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing how bad the idol was, explains why מיכה was not destroyed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מיכה's hospitality protected him from being destroyed.

steps.title: The tribes punished for ignoring מיכה's idol
steps.stepSummary: The people in the story of פילגש בגבעה were punished because they fought for a human's honor but never protested מיכה's idol, which insulted God's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for this the people in the story of פילגש בגבעה were punished. God said to them: You did not protest for My honor, but you protested for the honor of a human being!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the topic of מיכה by explaining that the tribes were punished for not protesting his idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tribes went to war over the wrong done to a person, but they had stayed quiet about idol worship near the משכן. God held them responsible for caring about human honor more than His honor.

keyTerms.meaning: the concubine in גבעה (the story in שופטים 19-20)
flesh and blood, a human being

steps.whatToRemember: מיכה himself was protected by his kindness, but the people who ignored his idol were punished for not standing up for God's honor.

phrases.english: And for this matter were punished
phrases.notes: 'This matter' means מיכה's idol, which no one protested.

phrases.english: the people of the concubine in Givah.
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them:
For My honor you did not protest,

phrases.aramaic: עַל כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל בָּשָׂר וָדָם מְחִיתֶם!
phrases.english: for the honor of flesh and blood you protested!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נֶעְנְשׁוּ אַנְשֵׁי פִּלֶגֶשׁ בַּגִּבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from מיכה's protection to the punishment of those who did not protest his idol.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tribes were punished in the war over פילגש בגבעה for not protesting מיכה's idol.

steps.title: Food is so powerful it pushed two nations away from ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יוסי בן קסמא, says לגימה (a mouthful of food) is so great that withholding it caused two families to be pushed away from ישראל, based on the פסוק about עמון and מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יוסי בן קסמא: A mouthful of food is a great thing, because it pushed two families away from ישראל. As the פסוק says: 'Because they did not greet you with bread and with water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about how important it is to give food. Not offering food had huge consequences for two nations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows naturally from the previous steps, where מיכה was protected because he fed travelers. Here we see the other side: עמון and מואב are kept out of ישראל because they did not offer bread and water. The proof is the reason the תורה itself gives for their exclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: A mouthful; giving someone food and drink
Families or clans; here, whole nations
Came forward to greet; met you ahead of time

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן קִסְמָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Kisma:
Great is a mouthful of food,
phrases.notes: לגימה literally means a gulp or mouthful. Here it means sharing food and drink with others.

phrases.english: for it distanced two families from Israel,
phrases.notes: The two families are עמון and מואב, the nations named in the פסוק being quoted.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עַל דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר לֹא קִדְּמוּ אֶתְכֶם
phrases.english: as it is stated: “Because they did not meet you
phrases.notes: דברים 23:5

phrases.english: with bread and with water.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן קִסְמָא גְּדוֹלָה לְגִימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea from step 32 that feeding travelers saved מיכה, now showing how withholding food brought a heavy punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving food is so important that failing to give it caused עמון and מואב to be kept out of ישראל.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's own list of five things food does
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in his own name, lists five effects of food: it distances the near, brings close the distant, makes God look away from the wicked, brings the שכינה onto the prophets of the בעל, and makes an accidental slip count as on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן himself said: Food pushes away those who are close, brings close those who are far, makes the eyes look away from the wicked, causes the שכינה to rest on the prophets of the בעל, and an accidental mistake with it counts as a deliberate sin.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי יוחנן gives a teaching in his own name: a list of five surprising things that food, or not giving it, can cause. The גמרא will explain each item next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier teaching gave only one result of food. Here רבי יוחנן widens it into five, some good and some bad. Each item is a short headline, and the proof for each one comes in the following lines.

keyTerms.meaning: His own; in his own name and not quoting someone else
Makes the eyes look away; causes punishment to be overlooked
An accidental sin / a deliberate sin

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's list has five parts. Keep them in order, because the גמרא now goes through them one by one.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a separate statement from the one before. In the first, רבי יוחנן was quoting רבי יוסי בן קסמא. Here he speaks in his own name (דידיה).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan himself says:
It distances the near,
phrases.notes: 'It' means food, the לגימה from the line before.

phrases.english: and draws near the distant,
and averts eyes from the wicked,
phrases.notes: He means it can make the wicked be overlooked, so they are spared punishment.

phrases.english: and causes the Divine Presence to rest on the prophets of the Baal,
and an unwitting mistake with it counts as intentional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 34's single effect of food into a list of five effects, in רבי יוחנן's own name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food has five powerful effects: it distances the near, draws near the distant, shields the wicked, brings the שכינה onto prophets of the בעל, and turns an accidental slip into a deliberate sin.

steps.title: Starting to explain the first item: food distances the near
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first item on רבי יוחנן's list, 'it distances the near,' so that it can explain where it comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It distances the near' —
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא repeats the first item from רבי יוחנן's list so that it can explain it in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is said yet. The repeated words act like a heading, marking the start of the explanation of each item. The source for this item comes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who are near or close

phrases.english: It distances the near —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the first item of רבי יוחנן's list from step 35 to begin explaining its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the explanation of the first effect of food: that it distances those who are near.
